era: Yemen's Civil War & the Fragile Truce (2014–2025)

events.title: Houthis Seize Sana'a
events.detail: On September 21, 2014, Houthi (Ansar Allah) fighters, backed by military units loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh, seized control of the capital Sana'a, forcing a power-sharing agreement and collapsing Yemen's post-Arab Spring political transition. Houthi forces continued advancing south over the following months, eventually placing President Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi under house arrest.

events.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Launches Operation Decisive Storm
events.detail: On March 26, 2015, Saudi Arabia led a nine-country coalition (UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Sudan) in launching airstrikes on Houthi positions after Houthi forces advanced on Aden, where Hadi had relocated. Backed by US intelligence, targeting assistance and logistics, the campaign was intended to restore Hadi's government within weeks but instead triggered a war that has now run for over a decade.

events.title: Stockholm Agreement Halts Battle for Hodeidah
events.detail: UN-brokered talks in Sweden produced a ceasefire for the Red Sea port of Hodeidah, a prisoner-exchange framework, and an understanding on Taiz, averting a full coalition assault on Yemen's main humanitarian lifeline port that aid agencies had warned could kill hundreds of thousands through starvation.

events.title: Drone and Missile Strikes Cripple Saudi Abqaiq-Khurais Facilities
events.detail: On September 14, 2019, simultaneous drone and cruise-missile strikes hit Aramco's Abqaiq processing facility and Khurais oil field, disrupting 5.7 million barrels per day — roughly half of Saudi production. The Houthis claimed the attack, but the US, UK, France, Germany and Saudi Arabia assessed the weapons and flight paths were inconsistent with a Yemen origin and blamed Iran directly. The episode became the founding case study for the air-defense buildup around Saudi oil infrastructure that shaped the Kingdom's 2026 response to renewed Jazan strikes.

events.title: UN Brokers Nationwide Truce
events.detail: A UN-mediated truce beginning April 2, 2022 halted coalition airstrikes and major Houthi cross-border attacks for the first time in years, permitted fuel ships into Hodeidah, and opened limited flights from Sana'a airport. Though the formal truce lapsed in October 2022 without renewal, both sides largely observed an informal de-escalation that held for nearly four years — until it collapsed in July 2026.

events.title: UN Estimates 377,000 Total War Deaths
events.detail: A UN Development Programme-commissioned study estimated the Yemen war had caused 377,000 deaths through the end of 2021 — roughly 60% from indirect causes such as food insecurity, lack of accessible healthcare and unsafe water, and the remainder from direct fighting. The Saudi-led coalition disputes the indirect-cause methodology; ACLED's direct-violence tally, using a narrower methodology, separately recorded the conflict surpassing 70,000 direct fatalities in earlier years. Both figures pre-date the 2026 escalation and are expected to be revised upward.
events.confidenceReason: Figure is contested on methodology (direct vs. indirect causes) and pre-dates the 2026 escalation.

events.title: US Launches Operation Rough Rider Air Campaign Against Houthis
events.detail: In March 2025 the White House authorized a sustained US air campaign — Operation Rough Rider — against Houthi targets in Yemen in response to Houthi attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea. The campaign continued for weeks and became the basis for a later Pentagon civilian-harm review released in August 2026 amid the wider 2026 escalation.

sources.name: Washington Post — Pentagon Yemen civilian toll report

events.title: US-Israel-Iran War Erupts, Destabilizing the Region
events.detail: The February 28, 2026 outbreak of direct US-Israel military action against Iran (Operation Epic Fury / Roaring Lion) destabilized the wider region. Iran-aligned armed groups — Hezbollah, Iraqi militias, and Yemen's Houthis — were drawn into supporting or solidarity actions, setting the stage for the Houthis to re-open fronts against both Israel and, eventually, Saudi Arabia.

events.title: Houthis Resume Attacks on Red Sea Shipping and Israel
events.detail: From March 3, 2026 the Houthis resumed drone and missile attacks on Red Sea shipping and fired ballistic missiles toward Israeli cities including Beersheba (Mar 28) and a claimed cluster-munition strike on Ben Gurion Airport (Apr 5), acting in declared solidarity with Iran. Saudi Arabia was not yet a direct target, but the group's expanded arsenal and operational tempo during this period built the capability later turned against the Kingdom.

sources.name: News on Air — Houthis enter war with missile strike on Israel
Al Jazeera — Houthi Red Sea attacks

events.title: Houthis End Four-Year Truce, Strike Abha Airport
events.detail: On July 13, 2026, Yemeni government forces backed by Saudi Arabia struck Sana'a airport's runway, reportedly to prevent an Iranian aircraft carrying a Houthi delegation from landing. Hours later the Houthis fired ballistic missiles and drones at Abha International Airport in Saudi Arabia's Asir region — their first claimed attack on Saudi soil since the informal 2022 truce. Saudi air defenses intercepted the projectiles with no casualties, but Houthi officials declared the 'de-escalation phase' over and threatened a 'siege' on the Kingdom.

events.title: Houthis Declare Maritime Blockade of Saudi Arabia
events.detail: On July 20, 2026 the Houthis announced a naval blockade against Saudi-linked shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, in retaliation for what they called the Kingdom's own blockade on Yemen and the Sana'a airport strike a week earlier. The declaration directly threatened the Kingdom's Red Sea export route via Yanbu, which had grown in importance as a diversification hedge against Strait of Hormuz risk from the Iran war.

events.title: Houthis Strike Two Saudi Oil Tankers, Brent Hits $100
events.detail: On July 23, 2026 the Houthis' SABA news agency said the group struck two Saudi-linked oil tankers — the Encelia and the Layla — in the Red Sea with a mix of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones, sparking fires on both vessels. No casualties were reported and all crew were reported safe. Brent crude jumped to $100/barrel for the first time since May, up roughly 40% for the month, as markets priced in a widening blockade.

events.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Strikes Houthi-Held Hodeidah
events.detail: On July 24-25, 2026 the Saudi-led coalition struck sites in and around Houthi-controlled Hodeidah and Sana'a for the first time since the 2022 truce, targeting military capabilities the coalition linked to the shipping and Aramco-facility attacks. The coalition said Hodeidah port itself was not targeted, seeking to avoid a repeat of the 2018 crisis over the port's role as Yemen's main aid lifeline.

events.title: First Houthi Strike on Aramco's Jazan Refinery
events.detail: On July 27, 2026 Houthi drones and missiles struck the gasification unit and tank farm at Aramco's 400,000 bpd Jazan refinery — the first direct Houthi attack on Saudi oil infrastructure of the 2026 escalation, and the first since the 2019 Abqaiq attack to again raise fears for Gulf energy security. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group also targeted Aramco facilities at Yanbu the same week. The refinery went offline in the aftermath.

sources.name: Al Jazeera — new front in Iran war

events.title: Saudi Arabia Launches 14-Nation Red Sea Maritime Defence Coalition
events.detail: Saudi Arabia convened 43 of 51 invited countries plus the EU in Riyadh on July 30, 2026 and launched a Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition. Fourteen states signed the founding statement — including Turkiye, Egypt, Pakistan, Jordan and Bangladesh — committing to intelligence sharing, joint exercises and maritime operations to protect Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Framed as purely defensive, the coalition notably did not include the UAE or Oman.

era: War Widens Into Yemen and Saudi Arabia — August 2026

events.title: Houthi Missile Barrage Kills Dozens of Government Troops in Marib, Hadramout
events.detail: On August 6, 2026 — the day this tracker begins — the Houthis fired eight ballistic missiles and drones from Al-Jawf governorate at military camps in Marib and Hadramout belonging to the Homeland Shield Forces, Emergency Forces and Yemen's First Military Region, catching troops gathered for a morning training exercise. Yemen's government confirmed at least 30 soldiers killed and 50 wounded; an unnamed military source told AFP the toll may have reached 58 dead. The Houthis claimed 45 killed. It was the deadliest single episode of the Yemen conflict in years and the clearest signal the informal 2022 truce had collapsed on the ground, not just at the border.
events.confidenceReason: Death toll contested: government says 30 killed/50 wounded, unnamed military source says up to 58, Houthis claim 45.

events.title: Najran Attack Wounds 11 as Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan Sign Mecca Defence Pact
events.detail: On August 7, 2026, Houthi projectiles struck the Saudi border city of Najran, wounding 11 civilians — 7 Saudis (including a woman and a 4-year-old with second-degree burns), 1 Yemeni, 2 Egyptians and 1 Pakistani — the highest civilian toll inside the Kingdom in over four years. The coalition called it an indiscriminate attack on civilian objects. The same day, MBS, Turkish President Erdoğan and Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, declaring an attack on any one signatory 'an attack against them all' — combining Pakistan's nuclear deterrent, Turkey's military-industrial base and Saudi financial resources into a hedge against reliance on the US.

events.title: Yemeni Government Forces Strike Back Amid Renewed Marib Shelling
events.detail: On August 8, 2026, Yemeni government forces began a counter-offensive against Houthi positions around Marib as shelling of the government-held oil city resumed. PLC Chairman Rashad al-Alimi said the legitimate government 'did not start the escalation and did not seek it,' but 'no action by the Houthi militias will go unanswered or unchecked,' rejecting any 'new truce that reproduces previous experiences.'

events.title: Second Houthi Drone Strike Hits Jazan Refinery; Port Attack Kills Seven
events.detail: A fire broke out before dawn on August 9, 2026 at Aramco's Jazan refinery after a Houthi drone strike — the second attack on the complex in under two weeks after the July 27 strike on its gasification unit and tank farm. Saudi authorities said the fire was extinguished by dawn with no injuries. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the strike 'succeeded in targeting the Aramco refinery in Jizan with a drone, and the strike was precise,' framed as retaliation for alleged Saudi drone incursions into Yemen's Saada and Hajjah governorates. The same day, a separate Houthi attack on a Yemeni port killed seven people.

events.title: Renewed Houthi Missile and Drone Attacks Kill Seven at Al-Makha
events.detail: On August 10, 2026 the Houthis renewed missile and drone attacks on Yemen's Red Sea port of al-Makha (Mokha), which government forces said killed seven people. The Houthis said they targeted buildups of weapons and warships belonging to Saudi-backed forces and 'mercenaries' at the port, destroying boats and weapons with a large number of ballistic missiles.

events.title: Houthi 'Double-Tap' Missile Strike Kills Six Near Bab al-Mandeb
events.detail: On August 11, 2026, the Houthis fired ballistic missiles at the cargo ship Tihamah — Tanzanian-flagged, owned by Egyptian and Yemeni interests — near Bab al-Mandeb. The strike killed four crew (three Pakistani, one Indonesian); a second missile then hit the search-and-rescue operation, killing two Yemeni coast guard rescuers and wounding several more. Yemen's government accused the Houthis of deliberately endangering rescuers. The Houthis claimed the ship carried Saudi military equipment, which was not independently confirmed. It marked the first fatal Houthi attack on shipping since the Iran war began February 28.

events.title: Pentagon Admits 153 Civilians Killed in 2025 Yemen Air Campaign
events.detail: A 12-page Pentagon review sent to the Senate Armed Services Committee and reported by the Washington Post on August 11, 2026 found that US forces killed 153 civilians and wounded nearly 250 others in three April 2025 attacks under Operation Rough Rider — the Trump administration's first public acknowledgment of significant civilian harm from its own military operations. The review found the strikes 'more likely than not' caused civilian harm but concluded none warranted condolence payments; 15 further incidents remain under investigation. Senators Van Hollen, Warren and Kaine pressed Defense Secretary Hegseth over the toll and the administration's rollback of civilian-harm safeguards.

sources.name: Sen. Tim Kaine — Yemen civcas letter

events.title: Houthis Announce New Strikes on Saudi Ship and Military Sites
events.detail: On August 13, 2026 the Houthis announced further strikes on a Saudi ship and military sites in the Red Sea, and said they had again targeted the Jazan refinery for a second time in under a week. Saudi-led coalition aircraft carried out reciprocal strikes on Houthi sites in Sana'a and Hodeidah, targeting military capabilities the coalition linked to the shipping and refinery attacks while stating Hodeidah port itself was not hit.

events.title: UN Envoy Warns Yemen Faces Highest War Risk Since 2022 Truce
events.detail: UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg warned the Security Council that 'Yemen today faces a greater risk of renewed large-scale conflict than at any point since the UN-brokered truce of April 2022,' as Al Jazeera analysis asked whether all-out war in Yemen was set to reignite amid the string of August strikes on Marib, al-Makha, Najran and Jazan.

sources.name: Security Council Report — Yemen August 2026 Monthly Forecast

events.title: Houthi Attack on Al-Makha Port Kills Four, Eroding Truce Further
events.detail: The Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of al-Makha on August 14, 2026. Yemen's government said the attack targeted civilian infrastructure and national assets, killing at least four civilians and setting several fishing boats ablaze; an unnamed government military official told AFP the toll reached at least eight, including two security personnel. The Houthis said they struck buildups of weapons and warships belonging to Saudi-backed forces at the port.
events.confidenceReason: Death toll disputed between government's initial count of 4 and an unnamed military official's count of 8.

events.title: Houthi Strikes Hit Residential Areas of Marib
events.detail: Yemen's government said on August 15, 2026 that Houthi strikes hit residential neighborhoods in Marib, a government-held city hosting more than two million displaced people. Yemen's Ministry of Information called the continued targeting of Marib's densely populated areas a dangerous escalation threatening civilian lives.

events.title: Houthis Fire Six Missiles Into Marib's Displacement Camps
events.detail: The Houthis fired six ballistic missiles and four drones into residential neighborhoods and displacement camps in Marib on August 16, 2026, wounding at least four people and damaging homes and civilian infrastructure. The same day, the Houthis launched new attacks on al-Makha as the wider conflict continued to escalate on both fronts.

events.title: Yemeni Armed Forces Say They Conducted 181 Operations Against Houthis in 24 Hours
events.detail: Yemen's Armed Forces spokesperson Col. Majed al-Nazili said on August 16, 2026 that government forces carried out 181 military operations against Houthi targets in the preceding 24 hours, using drones, artillery and rocket launchers to hit positions, weapons depots and vehicles across seven provinces and killing or wounding dozens of Houthi fighters. The government said the strikes were in response to the Houthis' wave of attacks on government forces, civilian infrastructure and ports.

media.caption: Yemeni government forces claim 181 operations against Houthi positions in 24 hours

events.confidenceReason: Single-sided government tally of strike counts and casualties; not independently verified.

events.title: UN Rights Chief Warns Yemen Risks 'Full-Scale Conflict', Cites 17 Civilian Deaths Since Aug 6
events.detail: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on August 17, 2026 that escalating conflict risked a return to full-scale war in Yemen, citing at least 17 civilians killed in Houthi attacks on government-controlled areas since August 6 — including a missile strike on the Jaw al-Naseem displacement camp in Marib (Aug 7, 6 wounded) and the Aug 9 Mokha port attack (3 port workers killed). 'I call on all parties to de-escalate tensions and spare the Yemeni people from further misery,' Türk said, warning that attacks on civilian infrastructure risk deepening suffering as at least 18 million Yemenis face food insecurity.

media.caption: UN rights chief Volker Türk warns of rising civilian toll in Yemen

events.title: Houthis Claim Ballistic Missile Strike on Saudi Landing Ship Off Mokha
events.detail: The Houthis said on August 17, 2026 they fired ballistic missiles at five Saudi vessels — a military landing ship and four escort patrol boats — near Mokha in the Red Sea. Spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the strike 'completely burned' the landing ship and left several escort boats sunk or ablaze. Yemen's Saudi-backed government disputed the target description, saying the vessel struck was a commercial ship that had been out of service for over a year and undergoing maintenance. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm any attack. The Houthis say they have fired more than 60 missiles and drones at Mokha since August 9.
events.confidenceReason: Single-source Houthi claim (spokesperson Yahya Saree); Yemeni government disputes the target's identity and status; no independent Saudi confirmation.

events.title: Houthis Renew Five-Hour Missile and Drone Barrage on Marib; Army Downs a Drone
events.detail: The Houthis targeted Marib with a barrage of ballistic missiles and drones from roughly 11:00 to 16:00 local time on August 18, 2026, with explosions and air-defense fire heard across the city; Yemeni army air defenses shot down at least one Houthi drone over the city. The same day, Yemen's Defense Council approved an expansion of the government's air and missile deterrence posture, citing recent government drone-strike operations against Houthi military positions.

media.caption: Houthi missile and drone barrage renews on Marib as army air defenses respond

events.title: Yemeni Army Claims Successful Operation South of Marib as Government Escalates
events.detail: Yemen's internationally recognized government announced on August 18, 2026 that its forces had conducted over 100 military operations against Houthi positions in the preceding 24 hours, and the Yemeni Army claimed a 'successful operation' against Houthi forces south of Marib. The National Defense Council raised the government's military readiness level and approved a permanent session, while PLC Chairman al-Alimi called for legal documentation of Houthi 'crimes' and urged the group to disarm and compete 'through the ballot box' instead.

events.title: War Risk Peaks: 15 Days of Escalation Since Marib-Hadramout Offensive
events.detail: As of August 20, 2026 — fifteen days since the Houthi offensive that killed dozens of Yemeni government troops in Marib and Hadramout — the conflict shows no sign of de-escalating. Houthi strikes have hit Najran, Jazan (twice), al-Makha (three times) and a claimed Saudi landing ship, while the Saudi-backed government has launched a counter-offensive around Marib backed by a newly raised National Defense Council posture and the 14-nation Red Sea Maritime Defence Coalition. UN Envoy Hans Grundberg's warning of the highest war risk since the 2022 truce remains the operative assessment; more than 22 million Yemenis need humanitarian assistance and the 2026 aid appeal is barely 20% funded.

events.title: Yemeni Government Forces Conduct 81 Operations Against Houthis in 24 Hours
events.detail: Yemen military spokesman Gen. Majid Abdullah al-Nuzaili said government-aligned forces carried out 81 operations against Houthi positions in the 24 hours to August 20, 2026, targeting fighters, field commanders, weapons depots and troop gatherings across multiple fronts and claiming to have 'neutralized' a number of Houthi fighters and commanders and destroyed military equipment. The government said the operations were a response to continued Houthi attacks on shipping and civilian facilities.

media.caption: Yemeni government forces say they conducted 81 operations against Houthi positions in 24 hours

events.confidenceReason: Government-reported operation and casualty count, not independently verified.

events.title: Houthis Claim Drone Strikes on Najran Airport and Aramco Facility
events.detail: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on August 20, 2026 the group 'successfully carried out two military operations using drones' — one targeting Najran Airport and a second targeting an Aramco facility in Najran province, framed as retaliation for alleged Saudi drone incursions over Yemen's Saada province. Saudi authorities and Aramco did not confirm the claims, and the Houthis provided no evidence of damage or casualties.

media.caption: Houthis claim drone strikes on Najran Airport and an Aramco facility

events.confidenceReason: Single-source Houthi claim; no Saudi or Aramco confirmation of damage or casualties.

events.title: IRGC Warns Saudi Arabia Cannot Contain the Houthis
events.detail: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesman Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi said on August 20, 2026 that 'Saudi Arabia will certainly be unable to contain Yemen and Ansarullah or remain safe from their attacks,' adding 'the more Saudi Arabia attacks, the more it is hit in return.' The statement came the same day the Houthis claimed the Najran drone strikes, underscoring Tehran's rhetorical backing for the group even as Iran continues to deny operational control over Houthi targeting decisions.

media.caption: IRGC spokesman warns Saudi Arabia cannot contain the Houthis

events.title: Armed Men Hijack Tanker Off Yemen, Divert Toward Somalia
events.detail: Six armed individuals boarded the tanker Seamull (also known as SIBU 1) roughly 136 nautical miles east of Yemen's al-Mukalla in the Gulf of Aden on August 20, 2026, taking control of the vessel and diverting it toward Somalia, the UK Maritime Trade Operations center (UKMTO) said. The tanker had previously been sanctioned by the US Treasury as part of Iran's 'shadow fleet' moving sanctioned petroleum products. The incident is part of a broader resurgence of Somali piracy in 2026 — the Gulf of Aden has recorded roughly 24 boarding/hijacking incidents in the past three months — compounding the security vacuum created by the Houthi-Saudi war and naval blockade.

media.caption: Armed men hijack the tanker Seamull off Yemen amid a resurgence of Somali piracy

events.title: Al-Makha Port Suspends Operations, 1,500 Workers Jobless
events.detail: Al-Makha (Mokha) port suspended operations around August 18, 2026 after weeks of repeated Houthi missile and drone strikes, leaving more than 1,500 port workers without income and idling 30 shipping and customs-clearance agencies. Port director Abdulmalik Al-Sharabi said the cumulative toll from the attacks reached 16 killed and 22 injured, with at least six merchant vessels struck. Traders are rerouting imports through Aden, raising logistics costs, while fishermen and residents describe a near-total halt to daily life — beaches, parks and the coastal walkway are closed, a nightly motorcycle curfew runs 11pm-6am, and landline/mobile communications in the area have been knocked out. The port is an economic lifeline for Taiz, Lahj, Hodeidah and Ibb.

media.caption: Idled cranes and empty berths at al-Makha port after Houthi strikes forced its closure

events.confidenceReason: Single-source Al Jazeera report citing the port director and local workers; casualty and job-loss figures not independently cross-verified by a second outlet.

events.title: Houthis Strike Saudi VLCC Supertanker Amzan Off Yanbu
events.detail: The Houthis fired an anti-ship ballistic missile at the Saudi-flagged VLCC Amzan — owned by state shipping giant Bahri and capable of hauling roughly two million barrels of crude — approximately 63 nautical miles west of Yanbu in the northern Red Sea early on August 24, 2026, while the vessel sailed from Egypt toward Yanbu. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the strike was 'precise and direct,' igniting a fire on the main deck and prompting nearby vessels to flee the area. Bahri confirmed a 'security-related incident' and said all crew were safe with no injuries or reported environmental damage. The Houthis framed the attack as part of their 'siege-for-siege' maritime ban on Saudi-linked shipping declared in mid-July. Market reaction was muted compared to July's tanker strikes, with Brent crude easing rather than spiking, as traders distinguished the contained vessel fire from a wider export-infrastructure shutdown.

media.caption: Saudi-linked vessels in the Red Sea have been attacked several times by the Houthis in the past month
